item.title: Application opens for 2026 Child Education Support Scheme, FENC Fiji targets 7,000 children
item.description: Children from families facing financial challenges will have an opportunity to receive education assistance under the 2026 Child Education Support Scheme, with applications and case reviews now open nationwide. The announcement was made by FENC Fiji Chief Executive Officer Priya Lata, who says the foundation is targeting between 6,800 and 7,000 children for assistance this year.
item.content:encoded:
Children from families facing financial challenges will have an opportunity to receive education assistance under the 2026 Child Education Support Scheme, with applications and case reviews now open nationwide.

The announcement was made by FENC Fiji Chief Executive Officer Priya Lata, who says the foundation is targeting between 6,800 and 7,000 children for assistance this year.

Lata says applications opened on 5th October and will close on 30th October.

She says FEN C Fiji has assisted more than 45,000 children across Fiji since it was established in 2009 and currently has more than 6,800 children on its programme.

Lata says staff will carry out face-to-face applications, reviews and home visits in the Northern and Western divisions, while parents in the Central and Eastern divisions can visit their nearest District Education Office.

She says new applicants must provide their child's birth certificate, school reports, a confirmation letter from the school and income verification.

Lata says additional documentation will be required from single or divorced parents, including certification from a Justice of the Peace.

She says applications will be vetted by volunteers, with priority given to families considered most in need.

Lata says the selection criteria includes families with a total income of $100 or less per week, single or divorced parents, grandparents caring for children, unemployed parents, families with sick parents and children with disabilities.

She says selected children will receive a school backpack containing books and stationery, while those starting Year 9 will also receive a calculator.

Lata says FENC Fiji may provide assistance with uniforms and shoes in extreme cases following an assessment of the family's circumstances.

For children already receiving assistance, she says parents will need to provide updated school reports and a report from the school headteacher.

Lata says the foundation uses these reports to verify attendance and punctuality and identify any difficulties a child may be facing, rather than judging children based on their academic results.

She says the number of children receiving assistance has increased from around 3,000 several years ago to more than 6,000 currently.

Lata says FENC Fiji has also dealt with cases where parents have falsified information or received assistance from multiple organisations.

She says such applications are terminated immediately, while cases involving falsified information may be reported to Police.

Lata says funding and reaching families in rural areas remain major challenges, particularly when families change their contact numbers or cannot be reached.

She is encouraging parents who are unable to contact the foundation to visit their nearest District Education Office.

Lata says assistance for children selected under the scheme is expected to be distributed from late December or early January.

item.title: Government must explain scholarship changes – Chand
item.description: Concerns are being raised over changes to Government scholarship opportunities, including overseas scholarships and scholarships for commercial pilot training. Opposition MP Hem Chand, who is calling on Government to explain the reasons and evidence behind the changes, says Year 13 students and parents deserve to know why the opportunities are being restricted and what alternatives will be availab
item.content:encoded:
Concerns are being raised over changes to Government scholarship opportunities, including overseas scholarships and scholarships for commercial pilot training.

Opposition MP Hem Chand, who is calling on Government to explain the reasons and evidence behind the changes, says Year 13 students and parents deserve to know why the opportunities are being restricted and what alternatives will be available to affected students.

He says he is particularly concerned about the removal of scholarships for commercial pilot training.

Chand says if Government's justification is that Fiji currently has enough trained pilots, it should explain why the number of scholarships was not simply reduced instead of removing the opportunity altogether.

He says workforce requirements can change and Fiji needs to consider its future aviation needs.

On overseas scholarships, Chand says students should continue to have opportunities to pursue specialised qualifications that are not available in Fiji.

He says this is especially important for Year 13 students who have worked hard with the expectation that strong academic performance would give them an opportunity to compete for merit-based scholarships.

Chand is also calling for data on sponsored students who have graduated and are meaningfully employed.

He says the private sector is struggling to find relevant graduates and questions whether the current scholarship allocation reflects Fiji's labour market needs.

Chand says more scholarships should be deliberately directed towards technical and vocational education and training, particularly in areas where there are skills shortages.

He says there is currently more emphasis on higher studies than TVET, which he describes as a labour market mismatch.

Chand is calling on Government to explain the workforce analysis behind the changes, what assistance will be available to affected students and how students seeking qualifications unavailable in Fiji will be supported.

He says scholarship policy should balance Fiji's workforce requirements with the aspirations of young people and should not simply close doors.

Meanwhile, the Tertiary Scholarships and Loans Service (TSLS) had earlier confirmed to fijivillage News that there will be no Pilot Training intake under the scholarship next year.

TSLS says the decision follows the significant number of scholarships awarded in recent years, with 59 students currently on active scholarships and more than 70 private students undertaking pilot training.

It says this is considered sufficient to meet Fiji Airways’ projected pilot intake requirements over the next few years.

Finance Minister Esrom Immanuel says the number of places is determined by demand and consultation with airlines.

Immanuel says Government will assess the need for 2027 and could increase the number of places if there is still a need.

He says the remaining pilot training places are privately funded.

item.title: Ledua’s lawyer challenges DNA evidence in RFMF armory case
item.description: Lawyer Jerry Dinati has informed the Suva High Court that his client, Isaia Ledua, was not informed of his rights when his DNA sample was taken. Ledua appeared before Suva High Court Judge Justice Dane Tuiqereqere, charged with one count of attempted aggravated burglary over allegations that he attempted to break into the RFMF armoury in Nabua between April 8th and 9th, damaging the door-lock keyp
item.content:encoded:
Lawyer Jerry Dinati has informed the Suva High Court that his client, Isaia Ledua, was not informed of his rights when his DNA sample was taken.

Ledua appeared before Suva High Court Judge Justice Dane Tuiqereqere, charged with one count of attempted aggravated burglary over allegations that he attempted to break into the RFMF armoury in Nabua between April 8th and 9th, damaging the door-lock keypad.

Justice Tuiqereqere directed the prosecution to provide further disclosures this week.

He also advised the parties to complete the necessary pre-trial processes ahead of the hearing.

The court has set aside two days for a voir dire hearing in April next year to determine whether the DNA evidence can be admitted at trial.

The matter has been adjourned to next Thursday for a pre-trial conference.
